title: Parquet/DuckDB pivot — the twelve-lane warehouse and its serving path
note: Chartered retroactively 2026-08-23: waves 1-3 already shipped (RUNBOOK 0.21-0.29) with no track, so the largest workstream in the repo was tracked only in prose. This records wave 4. The owner call behind it all is RUNBOOK 0.28/plantgeo-parquet-duckdb-pivot: Postgres keeps ONLY community features, every plane becomes day-partitioned Parquet on Railway storage read by DuckDB+Polars, Martin serves PMTiles. Map breakage during the transition is accepted.

partitions.note: HYPOTHESIS, not fact -- re-verify every owns list with a real grep if HEAD has moved past 3b7ecfb. z0 is the FOUNDATION and blocks everything: it changes foundation/parquet/paths.py, which every other slice imports, and it deliberately breaks every call site at type-check time. Run z0 ALONE, take its broken-call-site report, and only then fan out z1-z4. The prior partition set (computed at ef789f7) is superseded: its s1/s2 shipped, and s3/s4/s5 are re-scoped by the zoom axis.

slices.task: FOUNDATION, runs alone: add the zoom= partition key above year=, the uniform z0/z5/z9/z13 ladder, and a tier-resolution helper. Zoom is REQUIRED, never defaulted. No backward-compatible parse -- a path without zoom= must fail cleanly.
Teach the object store and the gap census the zoom axis: listing, pruning and coverage become per (layer, kind, zoom, day).
Tier derivation in Polars/DuckDB from the base Parquet -- never from Postgres matviews. Geometry generalization per ladder step.
Chunked streaming export, no row cap: delete MAX_SOIL_SURVEY_POLYGON_KEYS and batch to part-0..part-N so memory stays flat at any population.
The twelve planes/*.py readers take a zoom argument and resolve it through the ladder to a partition path.
interface/http serving API over the twelve planes: per-day, window, as-of, coverage; bbox pushdown; zoom routing; four-state provenance envelope.
